name: MO-08
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent advantage with no polling or expert attention
model.rationale: This is a deeply Republican rural Missouri seat with a well-funded incumbent, and the Democrat has raised almost nothing, so no evidence supports moving off the fundamentals. Markets and the absence of any ratings or polling both point to an easy Smith win.
model.watch: A surprise scandal or a major late outside-spending push against Smith would be the only realistic path to narrowing the race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Jason Smith seeks another term in a southeastern Missouri district that leans Republican by roughly 27 points. He enters the general election with about $5 million on hand, while Democrat Chris Reichard has raised under $6,000, leaving the challenger with essentially no resources to compete. A Libertarian is also on the ballot, further splitting the anti-Smith vote.

No public polls or expert ratings track the race, and prediction markets give Smith roughly a 96 percent chance of winning. The forecast rests on the district's strong partisan lean, Smith's incumbency and financial dominance, and the challenger's minimal campaign footprint, all pointing to a comfortable Republican hold.
